title: "Very" in Korean? I asked for ONE word… 😵 아주 · 정말 · 진짜 · 완전 #learnkorean
caption:
English has one "very." Korean has a whole pile.

The 4 you'll hear the most:
아주 (a-ju) — very
정말 (jeong-mal) — truly, really
진짜 (jin-jja) — really (casual, you'll hear it all the time)
완전 (wan-jeon) — totally (slang, with friends)

…and 8 more:
매우 (mae-u) — very (more written / formal)
너무 (neo-mu) — so (started as "too much," now used for "very" all the time)
엄청 (eom-cheong) — super
되게 (doe-ge) — really (casual)
무척 (mu-cheok) — very much
굉장히 (goeng-jang-hi) — extremely
몹시 (mop-si) — awfully
대단히 (dae-dan-hi) — greatly

They overlap a lot, and people mix them freely. New to Korean? Start with 진짜.

Try it: 한국어 진짜 어려워! (han-gu-geo jin-jja eo-ryeo-wo) — Korean is really hard!

alt: A needle-felted night study room. The coral felt mascot Mongle sits behind a desk with an open dictionary. Title: "Very" in Korean? Just one word… right? One felt tile reading 아주 (a-ju = very) pops out of the book — then the dictionary bursts. Felt word tiles fly out one by one with their meaning: 아주 (a-ju = very), 정말 (jeong-mal = truly), 진짜 (jin-jja = really), 완전 (wan-jeon = totally). Wait… even MORE words?! Eight more fly out in two groups of four: 매우 (very), 너무 (so), 엄청 (super), 되게 (really), then 무척 (very much), 굉장히 (extremely), 몹시 (awfully), 대단히 (greatly). Blank tiles pour down and fill the whole room until only Mongle's tired eyes peek out. Korean has a LOT of words for "very." Easiest one to start with: 진짜. A last 진짜 tile lands on Mongle's head. Mongle sighs: 한국어… 진짜 어려워… — Korean is 진짜 (= really) hard…
